execution.mechanism: klt sim --backend batch (2am EDA batch fleet, Spot)
execution.timing_note: elapsed_s per corner is the remote engine wall clock reported by klt (runtime_s). job_elapsed_s is the fleet harness's own job time. queue_provision_and_transfer_s = submit-to-collect wall minus job_elapsed_s (S3 upload, Spot acquisition/boot, polling granularity, download).

experiment.claim: spec/topology-survey.md Startup row ("self-starting, < 1 ms") -- the no-other-stable-state half, on the cell that would actually be fabricated. Substantiates that the ROUTED, LVS-clean bandgap-core layout (issue #62) -- which since issue #285 DRAWS design/startup_injector.sch inside the composed cell (MPC1, MPC2, MNS, MNI, MNC, QS) -- has exactly ONE DC operating point over the whole 0..VDD range of its startup node GDRV, and that the loop is pulled downhill by a bounded-below current everywhere in the degenerate region rather than merely somewhere in it. The DUT is the composed cell ALONE: this bench instantiates design/bandgap_core.sym with NO separate design/startup_injector.sym instance, because the extracted body already contains one, and it carries NO bare-core control instance, because the drawn cell cannot express one (issue #299 -- see the 'dropped measurements' note below for what that costs and where those claims still live). The extracted core comes from klt extract --parasitics translated to a simulatable netlist (sim/bin/post_layout_common.py), NOT design/bandgap_core.sch directly -- see 'Netlist provenance' below. The schematic-level counterpart of this claim, WITH its bare-core control, is sim/startup-stability/ (report row 8a); the startup TIME claim on this same composed cell is the sibling post-layout bench sim/startup-ramp-post-layout/; the +/-1% output-accuracy claim is issue #11.
experiment.provenance_source: layout/bandgap-core/reports/20260923-070209-dbd57a9/bandgap_core_routed.gds via `klt extract --parasitics` (layout record 20260923-070209-dbd57a9), translated by sim/bin/post_layout_common.py, over this bench's own sim/startup-stability-post-layout/testbench/tb_startup_stability_pl.sch
experiment.statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim)
experiment.title: Startup: the degenerate zero-current state is not an operating point of the COMPOSED LAYOUT CELL -- POST-LAYOUT (extracted netlist)

matrix.subset_reason: issue #16's Acceptance Criteria ask for issue #10's degenerate-state checks re-run 'at worst corners', not the full 45-point matrix sim/startup-stability's own schematic-level records use. This 8-point subset (process in {ff, ss} x temperature in {-40, 125} C x supply in {2.97, 3.63} V) is the temperature/supply extremes crossed with the two process corners sim/startup-stability/experiment.json's own notes field and sim/startup-ramp/experiment.json's vref_spread note identify as where this design's margin is thinnest: ff/125 C/3.63 V is the worst recorded dvref (+8.70 mV, record 20260803-204236-f41373d); the sibling startup-ramp bench's only two documented FAILs in its early records are both at ff/-40 C (2.97 V and 3.63 V, on vref_spread); ss is the slow-amplifier corner the same startup-ramp notes cite as the worst t_start_s (ss/125 C/2.97 V, +146 us against the 1 ms bound). tt/sf/fs and the 27 C / nominal-supply interior points are intentionally omitted -- they are not where the design's own prior evidence puts the degenerate-state margin at risk, and every one of them is already covered by sim/startup-time-post-layout's full 45-point matrix on the SAME extracted composed cell, whose 45/45 PASS (record 20260923-070906-dbd57a9, t_start 0.0678-0.1818 ms, gdrv_final 1.598-2.611 V) is the same 'the drawn injector evicts the degenerate state' statement measured transiently at every one of them. It also keeps this bench's cost bounded: each corner is four forced 251-point non-continuation DC sweeps over a parasitic-laden extracted netlist.

spread_checks.note: The startup node's operating voltage tracks the supply (GDRV ~ VDD - |Vgs_p|), so a multi-corner run must show it moving by more than the +/-10 % supply span. A flat vgdrv_dut across the matrix means the corner/supply knobs are not reaching the simulator.
Untrimmed output over process and temperature must move by more than 10 mV; a frozen value would indicate the .lib corner or .temp injection stopped taking effect.
